title: Deep Learning for Hyperspectral Video Object Tracking
Deep Learning for Hyperspectral Video Object Tracking
crossref.abstract: <jats:p>Hyperspectral video object tracking (HVOT) has garnered increasing attention in computer vision and remote sensing, as dense spectral signatures can significantly enhance object discrimination under camouflage, low contrast, and complex background interference. However, existing studies remain scattered across RGB transfer, multi-modal tracking, and hyperspectral-specific designs, and the systematic research and comparison is still lacking. In this article, a comprehensive research of deep learning for HVOT is presented. First, RGB video tracking paradigms and benchmarks are shown to establish the technical foundation, including correlation filters, Siamese networks, Transformers, RNNs, GANs, and other network architectures. Building upon this, core HVOT methodologies are systematically organized from distinct perspectives: prompt learning for data scarcity, band-domain gap adaptation, temporal information mining, and tracker prototypes, accompanied by a summary of HVOT benchmarks. Additionally, multi-modal video trackers and datasets are summarized to provide a broader crossmodal context. Furthermore, extensive experiments and analyses are conducted across the HOTC20, MSVT, MSSOT, MUST, HOTC23, and HOTC24 benchmarks. Through comprehensive evaluations, several consistent trends are revealed. Collectively, these findings indicate that robust HVOT remains an open and unresolved problem. To this end, persistent bottlenecks and promising research directions are discussed.</jats:p>
